title: RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) — Frame time vs FPS
description: Frame time in milliseconds is the honest metric: 16.7 ms is exactly 60 FPS, because FPS is just 1000 divided by frame time. RTSS leads with frame times because averages of FPS hide the stutters that frame times reveal.

title: RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) — Reading a frametime graph
description: The frametime graph plots every frame as a bar; flat means smooth, spikes mean stutter. Averages can claim 120 FPS while the graph shows regular 50 ms hitches — and the hitches are what your eyes actually feel.

title: RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) — Framerate limiter
description: The limiter caps the frame rate with precise pacing — 142 FPS on a 144 Hz display is the classic esports setting, staying just under the refresh to avoid vsync lag. Capping also cuts power draw and heat, since the GPU stops rendering frames nobody sees.

title: RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) — Scanline sync
description: Scanline sync is RTSS's low-lag tear-free mode: it synchronizes frame presentation to a chosen screen scanline instead of the full vsync barrier. One calibration per display finds the tearline, and then tearing hides in the overscan.

title: RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS) — 1% lows and session stats
description: RTSS can report 1% lows — the average of the worst one percent of frames — which is the number that describes real smoothness. A game at 144 FPS average with 40 FPS 1% lows stutters; the average alone would never tell you.
